form.subtitle: Choose what is backed up and when. Below you see right away what the next runs look like.

selector.label: Selection of applications

applications.label: Applications
applications.error: The applications could not be loaded.
applications.none: There is no application in the cluster yet.

labels.label: Namespace label
labels.hint: Format: key=value. Separate several with a comma; all of them must match.

cron.label: Cron expression
cron.hint: Five fields: minute hour day month weekday. For example * * * * * for every minute or */15 * * * * every 15 minutes.

timezone.label: Time zone
timezone.hint: The time applies in this time zone.

problems.name: Give the policy a name.
problems.cron: A cron expression has five fields separated by spaces.
problems.retention: Enter at least one number above 0 (whole numbers up to 1000).
problems.export: Choose at least one storage location so that the backups leave the cluster.

retention.label: Which backups stay?
retention.allHint: Nothing is ever deleted. Backups pile up until you delete them yourself.
retention.hint: Each number keeps the newest backup of each of the last hours, days, weeks, months or years. “The last” keeps the newest backups, whenever they were made. A backup stays when any rule keeps it. Everything else is deleted. Empty fields count as 0.

export.label: Storage locations
export.hint: Choose where each backup is also copied to: encrypted, without duplicate data, and from the second copy on only what changed. With no choice the backup stays in the cluster.
export.none: There is no storage location yet.
export.error: The storage locations could not be loaded.

preview.incomplete: Fill in the selection and the schedule and the next runs show up here.

locations.title: Storage locations
locations.subtitle: This is where your backups will be kept outside the cluster later. Add a location and test the connection.
locations.actionFailed: The action could not be carried out.

test.pendingHint: Restora is testing the connection. This usually takes a few seconds.

credentials_missing.text: The credentials for this location are missing.
credentials_missing.hint: Edit the location and enter the access key and the secret key again.

invalid_credentials.text: The storage rejected the access key or the secret key.
invalid_credentials.hint: Check both values for typos and whether the key is still valid. You can enter them again under Edit.

access_denied.text: The credentials are valid, but they may not do everything Restora needs in this bucket.
access_denied.hint: The key must be allowed to list, write, read and delete in the bucket.

bucket_not_found.text: This storage has no such bucket.
bucket_not_found.hint: Check the name of the bucket or create it with your provider.

endpoint_unreachable.text: Restora cannot reach the storage at this address.
endpoint_unreachable.hint: Check the address and the port, whether http or https is right and whether the cluster may reach the storage (firewall, DNS).

tls_error.text: The certificate of the storage is not trusted.
tls_error.hint: Use a certificate from a known authority. For tests only you can switch off the check of the certificate.

timeout.text: The storage did not answer in time.
timeout.hint: Check that the storage is reachable and not overloaded, then test again.

nfs_mount_failed.text: The NFS share cannot be mounted.
nfs_mount_failed.hint: Check the server and the path, whether the NFS server allows the nodes of the cluster and whether the nodes have an NFS client.

nfs_not_writable.text: The share is mounted, but Restora may not write there.
nfs_not_writable.hint: Allow the user with the number 65532 to write in the exported directory.

test_failed.hint: The technical details below help to find the cause.

unknown.hint: The technical details below help to find the cause.

protocol_mismatch.text: The address does not match the protocol of the storage.
protocol_mismatch.hint: Switch the address between http:// and https://. Self-hosted storage inside the cluster often uses http://.

empty.title: No storage location yet
empty.text: A storage location is a place outside the cluster where backups can be kept in addition later, for example an S3 bucket or an NFS share. Add one and check that the connection works.

error.title: Storage locations could not be loaded
error.text: Restora cannot read the list right now.
error.hint: Check that restora-api is running and may read in the cluster, then try again.

notFound.title: This storage location does not exist
notFound.text: It may have been deleted. Go back to the list.

delete.title: Delete storage location?
delete.intro: The storage location {{name}} will be deleted.
delete.forgets: Restora forgets the address and the stored credentials.
delete.keeps: Data that is already there is left alone.
delete.failed: The storage location could not be deleted.
delete.exports: {{n}} backups are kept there. They stay in the storage, but can no longer be restored from Restora.

errors.location_in_use: A policy still copies to this storage location. Take it out of the policy or delete the policy.

form.subtitle: After saving, Restora tests the connection and shows you the result.
form.testHint: For the test Restora creates a small test file, reads it and deletes it again.

endpoint.label: Address of the storage
endpoint.hint: With http:// or https://, for your own storage usually with a port. Without one, https is used.

bucket.label: Bucket
bucket.hint: The name of the bucket. It must exist already.

prefix.label: Folder in the bucket (optional)
prefix.hint: Restora keeps everything below this folder. Leave empty for the top level.

region.label: Region (optional)
region.hint: Needed for Amazon S3, usually empty for your own storage.

pathStyle.label: Address the bucket in the path
pathStyle.hint: Needed for MinIO and most self-hosted storage. Amazon S3 does not need it.

skipTLS.label: Do not check the certificate
skipTLS.hint: For tests with a self-signed certificate only.
skipTLS.warning: Without the check, somebody can pose as your storage. Do not use this for real data.

keys.hint: Restora stores the credentials as a Kubernetes secret. They are not visible anywhere afterwards.
keys.keepHint: The stored credentials are kept. Fill in both fields only if you want to replace them.

nfs.hint: The cluster mounts the share itself. The user with the number 65532 must be allowed to write there.

path.label: Path
path.hint: The exported directory on the server, for example /exports/restora.

problems.name: Give the storage location a name.
problems.endpoint: Enter the address of the storage.
problems.bucket: Enter a valid bucket name: 3 to 63 lowercase letters, digits, dots or hyphens.
problems.path: Enter the path with a slash at the start.

dialog.title: Restore application?
dialog.intro: The application {{application}} will be reset to the state of the backup of {{time}}.
dialog.volumes: The volumes {{volumes}} will be deleted and created again from the backup. Everything written since this backup is lost.
dialog.noVolumes: This backup has no volumes. Only the saved resources are applied.
dialog.resources: {{resources}} saved resources will be applied. Resources with the same name in the application are overwritten.
dialog.downtime: Programs that use these volumes are stopped and started again afterwards. The application is unavailable meanwhile.
dialog.startFailed: The restore could not be started.

snapshot_not_ready.text: This backup is not complete and cannot be restored.
snapshot_not_ready.hint: Pick a backup that finished successfully.

restore_in_progress.text: A restore of this application is already running.

snapshot_in_progress.text: A backup of this application is running right now.
snapshot_in_progress.hint: Wait until it has finished, then restore.

cluster_unreachable.text: Restora could not start the restore.
cluster_unreachable.hint: Check that restora-api may create restore requests and that the cluster is reachable.

application_missing.text: The application's namespace no longer exists.
application_missing.hint: Create the namespace again, then restore. Restoring into a deleted namespace will follow later.

volume_snapshot_missing.text: A snapshot of the volumes was deleted outside of Restora or is not usable.
volume_snapshot_missing.hint: This backup cannot be restored. Check the storage driver.

export_missing.text: The saved settings of this backup can no longer be read.
export_missing.hint: The Restora data volume lost the files. This backup cannot be restored.

volume_in_use.text: A pod uses a volume that must be replaced, but it does not belong to a Deployment or StatefulSet.
volume_in_use.hint: Stop or delete this pod yourself, then start the restore again. Nothing has been changed yet.

timeout.text: The restore did not finish in time.
timeout.hint: Check that the application's pods stop and that the storage driver can create volumes from snapshots. Then start a new restore. The backup is unchanged.

workloads_not_ready.text: The data is restored, but the application did not start in time.
workloads_not_ready.hint: Look at the application's pods and events. The backup itself is unchanged.

unknown.hint: The technical details below help to find the cause. The backup is unchanged, so you can try again.

repository_key_missing.hint: Restore the secret restora-repo-… from a copy of the key. Nothing has been changed yet.

repository_password_invalid.text: The key of this cluster does not fit the storage location.
repository_password_invalid.hint: Restore the right key in the secret restora-repo-…. Nothing has been changed yet.

location_missing.text: The storage location of this backup does not exist any more.
location_missing.hint: Add the storage location again. Nothing has been changed yet.

credentials_missing.text: The credentials of the storage location are missing.
credentials_missing.hint: Edit the storage location and enter the credentials again.

bundle_missing.text: The saved settings of the application cannot be read in the storage location.
bundle_missing.hint: This backup is incomplete. Choose another one.

mover_not_started.text: The pod that brings the data back does not start.
mover_not_started.hint: Check that the cluster may start pods in the namespace of the application and that the image of Restora can be pulled.

access_denied.hint: Test the storage location and check the rights of the key.

bucket_not_found.text: The bucket does not exist any more.
bucket_not_found.hint: Test the storage location and check the name of the bucket.

endpoint_unreachable.text: The storage cannot be reached from the nodes of the cluster.
endpoint_unreachable.hint: Test the storage location and check the address, the network and the firewall.

nfs_not_writable.text: The NFS share does not allow access for the restore.
nfs_not_writable.hint: The restore runs as root. The share must not squash root (no_root_squash).

snapshot_not_in_repository.text: This backup is not (any more) in the storage location.

export_failed.text: Bringing the data back from the storage location failed.

repository_password_invalid.hint: There already is an archive of another Restora. Use an empty folder in the bucket (folder in the bucket) or restore the key of that archive in the secret restora-repo-….

access_denied.hint: Test the storage location and check the rights of the key: it must be allowed to write, read and delete.

bucket_not_found.text: The bucket does not exist any more.
bucket_not_found.hint: Test the storage location and check the name of the bucket.

endpoint_unreachable.text: The storage cannot be reached from the nodes of the cluster.
endpoint_unreachable.hint: Test the storage location and check the address, the network and the firewall. The copy runs in a pod next to the application.

nfs_not_writable.text: The NFS share does not let the copy write.

location_missing.text: The storage location does not exist any more.
location_missing.hint: Choose another storage location in the policy.

credentials_missing.text: The credentials of the storage location are missing.
credentials_missing.hint: Edit the storage location and enter the access key and the secret key again.

bundle_missing.text: The saved settings of this backup can no longer be read.

mover_not_started.text: The pod that copies the data does not start.

export_unavailable.text: This version of Restora cannot copy to storage locations.

export_failed.text: The copy to the storage location failed.
export_failed.hint: The technical details below help to find the cause. The local backup is fine.

unknown.text: The copy to the storage location failed.
unknown.hint: The technical details below help to find the cause. The local backup is fine.

card.title: Backups in storage locations
card.intro: These copies are kept outside the cluster. You can restore the application from them, even when the local backup or the whole namespace is gone.

error.title: Stored backups could not be loaded
error.text: Restora cannot read the list right now. Try again.

deleted.text: This application does not exist in the cluster any more. Its backups are still in storage locations. You can restore it from there: Restora creates the namespace again and brings back volumes and settings.

setup.title: Setup
setup.subtitle: Four steps from a fresh installation to a backup that is proven to come back.

error.title: The state of the setup could not be read
error.text: Restora cannot query the cluster right now. Try again.

location.title: Where should the backups go?
location.intro: Backups inside the cluster are lost with the cluster. Add a storage location outside, for example an S3 bucket or an NFS share. After saving, Restora tests the connection and moves on by itself as soon as it works.

policy.title: When and what is backed up?
policy.intro: A policy backs up on a schedule and copies each backup to the storage location. The suggestions fit for a start: all applications, every night at 2 am. You can change everything later, including the retention.

run.title: Trial run: back up once now
run.intro: Restora now backs up {{applications}} and copies the backup to the storage location. Depending on the size this takes one to a few minutes. You see here how it goes.
run.noApplications: No application matches the policy right now. Start an application or change the selection of the policy.
run.startFailed: The trial run could not be started.

restore.title: Check that the restore works
restore.intro: A backup that was never restored is only a hope. Restora now brings {{application}} back from the storage location and so checks the whole way: location, key and data.
restore.warning: Careful: this replaces the volumes of {{application}} with the trial backup. Everything written since the trial run is lost. The application is briefly unavailable. If you do not want that, skip this step.

done.title: All set
done.text: The backup runs on a schedule, lands encrypted in the storage location and is proven to be restorable. Restora does the rest.

banner.title: Set up Restora
banner.text: Step {{n}} of {{total}}: {{name}}. The setup takes a few minutes.

settings.title: Setup assistant
settings.text: Takes you in four steps from the installation to the first backup that is proven to come back.
